item.title: Eight states sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT isn’t safe for kids
item.description: OpenAI is facing a new wave of lawsuits from eight US states that accuse the company of harming children and misleading customers about the safety of ChatGPT, as reported earlier by Reuters. The lawsuits, filed separately by Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana, allege OpenAI unlawfully put profits over safety when […]...

item.title: Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 6 business laptop review
item.description: The ThinkPad T14s Gen 6 (AMD) is a stylish, well-built laptop that's designed for real-world productivity. And, yes, the keyboard is still best-in-class.

item.title: Trump Aides Admit the House is a Lost Cause
item.description: With the midterm elections just a few weeks away, the White House knows it has to go all in on Senate races—while virtually forfeiting the House.

item.title: Colossal Biosciences announces new AI platform to help accelerate de-extinction efforts
item.description: Colossal announced a new AI platform to help accelerate its de-extinction efforts and Peter Diamandis has launched a new fund to back startups who use it.

item.title: 'Nothing is obvious and nothing is rubbed into your face' — Control Resonant composer says 'in the end it’s all only music made with love and enthusiasm' and fans will likely uncover hidden easter eggs in the soundtrack years later
item.description: Control Resonant composer Petri Alanko has revealed that his music features easter eggs that may take fans years to uncover.

item.title: I've tried Apple's HomeView, and it could help me do more at home without reaching for my iPhone
item.description: I've spent some time with Apple's HomeView smart display, exploring its personalized interface, smart home controls, and new Siri AI features. It could finally bring Apple's ecosystem together and help me reach for my iPhone less often, but Siri still has some work to do.

item.title: Flock CEO: We haven’t ‘fired’ any police departments as customers
item.description: Flock CEO Garrett Langley said that the surveillance company has not canceled contracts of any police department or law enforcement agency, despite reports of abuse.

item.title: Fitbit Edge vs Fitbit Air: The differences beyond a screen
item.description: Google's latest wearable seems like a Fitbit Air with a screen, but the two actually have less in common than you might think.

item.title: Electric vehicle sales in the US are showing signs of life
item.description: The electric vehicle market in the U.S. has been growing for the last three consecutive quarters.

item.title: I recommend these SwissGear suitcases to anyone who asks — and theyre up to 35% off on Amazon
item.description: SwissGear's two-piece Energie Spinner Luggage Set is on sale on Amazon for up to 35% off. Choose from gunmetal or white colorways.

item.title: NASA explains how it's making batteries for the Moon's extreme temperatures
item.description: Lithium-ion just isn't cut out for the cosmos.

item.title: Microsoft and Japan took down a cybercrime network behind over a billion scam messages
item.description: We've all gotten a scam text about a nonexistent parking ticket or a fake package delivery, but hopefully you'll start seeing fewer of them. Microsoft says it helped dismantle a marketplace for scammers sending phishing messages like those around the world. Through an investigation with Japan's National Police Agency, it tracked scam activity back to […]...

item.title: TimeTeller puts our internal clocks at the center of personalized medicine
item.description: German startup TimeTeller has developed a saliva test kit to help anyone understand their circadian rhythm; it aims to reduce side effects from cancer treatments.

item.title: Hood Warfare 2, a $5 gang shooter on Steam, is going viral
item.description: Hood Warfare 2, a $5 Steam shooter set in Chicago, went viral this week.

item.title: Delta One’s new ultra-luxury suites come with Wagyu beef burgers and a $200 bottle of wine
item.description: As airlines court high spenders, Delta is upping the premium stakes with the first major holistic redesign of its kind in 30 years. For the average traveler, flying at 30,000 means tight seats and dried-out peanuts—not exactly luxury.

item.title: Ambrosia Energy will build a 10 GWh factory in Texas to make batteries for off-grid data centers
item.description: Startup Ambrosia Energy will build a massive factory to crank out batteries to augment solar panels, creating a round-the-clock clean power plant.

item.title: GTA 6 Cyberleek update: Leaker linked GTA 6 reveals to crypto play. It’s crashing spectacularly.
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI leakers failed to hit memecoin goal and will hold off on releasing the game.

item.title: The first new sunscreen type in 25 years hits U.S. store shelves
item.description: Sunscreens containing bemotrizinol (BEMT) have decades of safety data, including studies showing minimal absorption into the skin. For the first time in more than a quarter-century, Americans have a new option when shopping for sunscreen: a skin-protecting chemical that’s long been a go-to option in Europe and other parts of the world.

item.title: Water-resistant and easy to clean: HP delivers an AMD Ryzen keyboard PC that can be splashed with liquid — EliteBoard G1a has a 32Whr battery but alas no touchpad, review finds
item.description: HP put a full Ryzen PC inside a keyboard - the catch is the €2,149 price tag.

item.title: Ubisoft plans to close another studio and lay off up to 122 workers
item.description: Cuts are coming to RedLynx and Ubisoft Singapore.
